bundle.title: Let staff cancel an unbooked SMS send on its send day
bundle.body:
Campaign success staff could not cancel outreach 85286 from the SMS console today. The button spun and nothing happened. Loki shows three `POST /v1/outreach/admin/sms/85286/cancel` calls, all 400 with "Only scheduled campaigns can be canceled". The send day is today, and the Peerly job was never booked (paused, no canvassers scheduled), so nothing was sending.

Why it refused: the hourly completion sweep moves a p2p row from `pending` to `in_progress` at the UTC start of its send day, whether or not anyone booked it. `cancelOutreach` accepted only `pending`, and it ran that check before the rule that an unbooked row past its date stays cancelable (added after QA 2026-09-10, prod outreach 81412). So the sweep defeated that rule on exactly the day staff need it. Deny already accepts `in_progress` for this reason. The hold-model cancel (`OutreachP2pSmsCancelService`) had the same check, and its spine flip was guarded on `pending`/`pending_payment` as well, so it is fixed the same way.

Cancel now accepts an `in_progress` p2p row only when it was never booked (`approvedAt` and `canvassRequestedAt` both null). A booked row past its send time, a booked `in_progress` row and a `completed` row are still refused. The claim CAS also checks that the row is still unbooked, so an approve that lands mid-cancel wins. A failed cancel now restores the status the row was claimed from instead of forcing `pending`. The wider rule applies to p2p only, because a Serve text reads `in_progress` once its delivery handoff has claimed the send, and that claim has to keep refusing a cancel.

This guard is shared with the candidate-side cancel (`POST /v1/outreach/:id/cancel`). That is intended: a candidate whose unbooked send reaches its day gets the same refund and promo return that staff can now give them.

On the console side, `cancelSms` threw, Next redacts a thrown server-action message in prod, and the admin toast viewport was unstyled, so it rendered behind the AlertDialog overlay or below the fold. The action now returns the failure as data (the `resendCvPin` pattern), the dialog shows gp-api's own message inline, and the toast viewport is fixed above dialogs so every gp-admin toast is visible.

Follow-up, not in this PR: `approveSms`, `denySms`, `editSmsDate`, `editSms` and `sendTestSms` still throw, so their failures are swallowed in prod the same way.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches cancel eligibility, refunds, and status CAS/revert paths for paid outreach; mistakes could refund in-flight sends or block legitimate cancels.
> 
> **Overview**
> Staff could not cancel **unbooked** p2p campaigns on their send day because the completion sweep moves them to `in_progress` while cancel only accepted `pending`. **gp-api** now treats **unbooked** p2p rows in `in_progress` like pending (refund/delete job, promo restore); **booked** `in_progress`, Serve `text`, and completed sends stay refused. The cancel CAS claims from the row’s real status and **reverts to that status** on failure instead of always `pending`.
> 
> **gp-admin** `cancelSms` returns `{ error }` (gp-api messages survive prod server-action redaction). **CancelAction** shows failures in the confirm dialog; unexpected rejections go to Sentry. **Toast** viewport is fixed above dialogs so success toasts are visible.
>

**Race: satellite cancel deletes the Peerly job without an atomic claim on the spine.**

The satellite cancel path reads the spine at line 144 for eligibility, then proceeds to delete the vendor job (line 183) and release the hold (line 186) with no CAS in between. A concurrent staff approve landing after the eligibility read but before the job delete can book the row (`approvedAt` set), and the cancel proceeds anyway — deleting the vendor job for a now-booked send. `markSpineCanceled` (which correctly filters `approvedAt: null`) then becomes a no-op, leaving the spine stuck in `in_progress` with no vendor job and money already refunded.

The shared `cancelOutreach` path in `outreach.service.ts` (lines 1211-1225) guards against exactly this race with an `updateMany`-as-CAS that atomically claims the row (filtering on `approvedAt: null, canvassRequestedAt: null`) before any side-effecting work. The satellite path has no equivalent guard.

The new `in_progress` unbooked support added in this PR directly widens the exploitable window, because unbooked `in_progress` rows are the most frequent target for concurrent approve.

Falsification check: confirmed by reading both files in full — the satellite cancel path has no CAS claim on the spine before the Peerly job delete at line 183; the shared `outreach.service.ts` path at lines 1211-1225 shows the correct pattern with an explicit atomic claim that includes `approvedAt: null`, which is absent in the satellite path.
